concepts.name: Kutiyattam: UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage Status and Structural Features
key_dimensions: Only classical theatre form of India recognized by UNESCO (2008) — a frequent UPSC trap distinguishing it from other UNESCO-listed performing arts
Sanskrit theatre tradition of Kerala performed exclusively in 'Kuttambalam' (temple theatre) — spatial and ritual exclusivity
Role of Chakyar (performer) and Nangyar (female performer) castes — hereditary and caste-bound transmission
Angika (body language), Vachika (speech), Aharya (costume), and Sattvika (emotional expression) — Natyashastra's fourfold acting framework applied

concepts.name: Natyashastra by Bharata Muni: Foundational Framework for Indian Classical Theatre
key_dimensions: Concept of 'Navarasa' (nine emotions) — UPSC traps on whether 'Shanta' rasa was original or later addition by Abhinavagupta
Distinction between Natya (drama), Nritya (expressive dance), and Nritta (pure dance) — definitional overlaps tested
Theory of 'Rasa-Dhvani' (suggestion of emotion) — philosophical underpinning connecting theatre to aesthetics
Natyashastra as the 'fifth Veda' — accessible to all four varnas, unlike the first four Vedas — social significance angle

concepts.name: Kathakali: Classical Dance-Drama of Kerala — Origins, Conventions, and Misclassifications
key_dimensions: Evolved from Krishnanattam and Ramanattam — distinguishing lineage from Kutiyattam (a common UPSC confusion trap)
Navavidha Abhinaya (nine types of expression) and elaborate Chutti (face makeup) color-coding system — green for heroic, black for evil
Exclusively male performers historically — gender conventions and modern exceptions
Performed overnight in temple courtyards — ritual context versus contemporary stage adaptations

concepts.name: Yakshagana: Classical Theatre of Karnataka — Regional Identity and Structural Duality
key_dimensions: Two distinct styles: Tenkutittu (southern style) and Badagutittu (northern style) — geographical subdivision often tested
Integration of Prasanga (script), Bhagavata (narrator-singer), and Veshadhari (actor) — tripartite structural convention
Mythological themes from Mahabharata, Ramayana, and Puranas — thematic scope and social function
Distinction from Bayalata (open-air theatre of Karnataka) — overlapping regional traditions trap

concepts.name: Therukoothu (Terukkuttu): Tamil Street Theatre — Sacred and Secular Dimensions
key_dimensions: Performed in open streets (Theru = street) — spatial distinction from temple-bound forms
Associated with Draupadi cult temples — ritual function tied to goddess worship
18-day performance cycle linked to Mahabharata episodes — thematic and temporal structure
UNESCO recognition consideration and overlap with Koothu forms — classification traps

concepts.name: Chhau Dance-Theatre: Tribal, Folk, and Classical Overlap — Three Regional Variants
key_dimensions: Three sub-styles: Seraikella (Jharkhand), Purulia (West Bengal), Mayurbhanj (Odisha) — only Purulia and Seraikella use masks; Mayurbhanj does not — a classic UPSC trap
UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage (2010) — listed as 'Chhau dance' not theatre, classification nuance
Martial arts (Paika) influence on movement vocabulary — martial-performance continuum
Transition from folk to classical recognition — Sangeet Natak Akademi's role in codification

concepts.name: Ankiya Nat and Bhaona: Vaishnavite Theatre Tradition of Assam
key_dimensions: Founded by Srimanta Shankardev in 15th–16th century — Bhakti movement's direct theatrical expression
Performed within Namghar (prayer hall of Satra) — institutional and spatial context of Vaishnavite monasteries
Use of Sutradhara (stage manager-narrator) — a role traceable directly to Natyashastra
Distinction between Ankiya Nat (script/text) and Bhaona (performance) — text vs. performance duality often confused

concepts.name: Koodiyattam vs. Krishnanattam vs. Kathakali: Distinguishing Kerala's Classical Theatre Forms
key_dimensions: Koodiyattam (Kutiyattam): Sanskrit, temple-bound, UNESCO listed — oldest living Sanskrit theatre
Krishnanattam: Sanskrit, performed only at Guruvayur Temple — geographically and institutionally restricted, not UNESCO listed
Kathakali: Malayalam-based, derived from Krishnanattam — open performance, no temple restriction
UPSC trap: Krishnanattam's exclusivity to one temple — 'only' clause makes it highly examinable

concepts.name: Ramleela and Raasleela: Epic Theatre Traditions — UNESCO Status and Regional Variations
key_dimensions: Ramleela of Ramnagar (Varanasi) inscribed on UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage list (2008) — specific regional form, not all Ramleela performances
Raasleela associated with Braj region (Mathura-Vrindavan) — Krishna-centric versus Ram-centric distinction
Ramleela as community participatory theatre — audience as active participant, not passive spectator
Distinction between Ramleela (folk-classical hybrid) and Ramlila as political spectacle — contemporary relevance

concepts.name: Sangeet Natak Akademi: Institutional Role in Classical Theatre Preservation
key_dimensions: Established in 1952 — India's first national academy of the arts, predating Sahitya and Lalit Kala Akademis
Autonomous body under Ministry of Culture — not a statutory body, a registered society — governance trap
Awards Sangeet Natak Akademi Fellowships (Ratna Sadsya) — highest honor, limited to 40 living fellows at a time
Role in documentation, transmission grants, and Guru-Shishya Parampara schemes for classical theatre

concepts.name: Maach Theatre of Madhya Pradesh: Structure and Sufi-Bhakti Synthesis
key_dimensions: Originated in Ujjain in 19th century — associated with Gopal Ganesh Upadhyay
Elevated stage (Maach = stage/platform) with no front curtain — spatial and structural uniqueness
Blend of Sufi, Bhakti, and local folklore themes — syncretic cultural content
Role of Rangabhoomi (performance space) and Ranga (director-narrator) — structural parallels with Sutradhara in Sanskrit theatre

concepts.name: Tamasha: Classical-Folk Theatre of Maharashtra — Social Critique and Gender Conventions
key_dimensions: Lavani as the musical backbone — distinction between Tamasha (theatre form) and Lavani (musical genre within it)
Murki (female performer) and Songadya (male clown) — gender and comedic role conventions
Historical association with Peshwa-era military camps — origins as entertainment for soldiers
Social reform themes — Annabhau Sathe's contribution in using Tamasha for Dalit assertion

concepts.name: Jatra: Bengal's Classical Folk Theatre — Epic Scale and Political Dimensions
key_dimensions: No stage separation — audience surrounds performers on all four sides (thrust stage) — spatial convention
Vivek (conscience character) — unique dramatic device representing the protagonist's inner moral voice, exclusive to Jatra
Role during Bengal Renaissance and nationalist movement — Girish Chandra Ghosh's contributions
Distinction between traditional Jatra (mythological) and post-independence Jatra (social-political themes)

concepts.name: Bharatanatyam vs. Kuchipudi: Overlapping Classical Forms — Theatre Origins of Both
key_dimensions: Kuchipudi originated as a theatre tradition (Kuchipudi village, Andhra) before becoming a solo dance form — theatrical origin often neglected
Bharatanatyam's devadasi tradition and Rukmini Devi Arundale's role in its 'classicization' — reform and reinvention
Both trace lineage to Natyashastra — but Kuchipudi retains Yakshagana-style narrative episodes (Yakshagana is a separate form — a trap)
Male brahmin performer tradition in Kuchipudi versus female devadasi tradition in Bharatanatyam — gendered performance history

concepts.name: Sanskrit Theatre Conventions: Sutradhara, Vidushaka, and Nati — Dramaturgical Roles
key_dimensions: Sutradhara (stage director-narrator) — 'holder of the strings,' connects to Natyashastra's stage management theory and ironically links to puppetry etymology
Vidushaka (court jester/fool) — Brahmin character speaking Prakrit while others speak Sanskrit — linguistic-class inversion as social commentary
Nati (actress) — female performer whose social status in ancient India versus modern classical revival — historical-contemporary contrast
Purvaranga (pre-performance ritual) versus Nandi (benedictory verse) — structural conventions tested for sequence and purpose

concepts.name: Manipuri Sankirtana: Music-Theatre-Ritual Continuum and UNESCO Recognition
key_dimensions: UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage (2013) — as 'Sankirtana, ritual singing, drumming and dancing of Manipur'
Associated with Vaishnavism introduced by King Bhagyachandra in 18th century — historical patronage context
Distinction between Sankirtana (ritual performance) and Manipuri classical dance — a common misclassification
Pung (barrel drum) and Kartal (cymbals) as defining instruments — material culture angle

concepts.name: Mudiyettu: Ritual Theatre of Kerala — Caste, Ritual, and UNESCO Listing
key_dimensions: UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage (2010) — performed exclusively by Marar and Kurup communities — hereditary caste restriction
Depicts battle between goddess Bhadrakali and demon Darika — mythological-ritual function
Performed only in Bhagavati temples of central Kerala — geographic and sacred space restriction
Distinction from Theyyam (another ritual performance of Kerala) — Mudiyettu is theatre/drama; Theyyam is possession ritual — classification trap

concepts.name: Theyyam vs. Mudiyettu vs. Padayani: Kerala's Ritual Performance Spectrum
key_dimensions: Theyyam: North Kerala, performer becomes deity (possession), not considered classical theatre — Malabar region specificity
Mudiyettu: Central Kerala, performers enact mythological narrative without possession — theatrical distinction from Theyyam
Padayani: South Kerala (Pathanamthitta), kolam (mask) tradition, associated with Bhadrakali worship — geographic-ritual layering
UPSC trap: All three involve Bhadrakali but differ in region, method, and classification (theatre vs. ritual)

concepts.name: Dashavatar: Goa-Konkan Classical Theatre — Vaishnava Narrative and Performance Space
key_dimensions: Ten avatars of Vishnu as structural framework — title reflects Vaishnava theological content
Performed in temple complexes of Goa, Konkan Maharashtra, and coastal Karnataka — cross-state regional identity
Intricate masks and costumes representing different avatars — material culture and iconographic dimension
Distinction from Dashavatar folk performances of other regions — regional specificity trap (e.g., Dashavatar of Uttar Pradesh is a different tradition)

concepts.name: Zatra (Odia Jatra) and Prahlada Nataka: Odisha's Classical Theatre Spectrum
key_dimensions: Prahlada Nataka of Ganjam district — performed by Ganda (weaver) community — community-specific performance tradition
Distinction between Odia Jatra (narrative theatre) and Bengali Jatra — similar names, distinct traditions — a major UPSC confusion trap
Thematic focus on Vaishnava mythology and Panchasakha philosophy — theological underpinning
Pala (narrative singing) as a parallel Odia classical performance tradition — overlapping forms within one state
